title: More Japanese Teens Getting Cosmetic Surgery
paragraphs: Cosmetic surgery is becoming more common among young people in Japan — even among those as young as junior high school age.

A recent report from Jiji Press shared information from Kyoritsu Cosmetic Surgery, which runs 17 clinics in Tokyo's Shibuya area, a popular youth hotspot. Kyoritsu said people aged 19 or younger made up just 7% of its patients in 2017. By 2025, this had risen nearly three times, to 19%.
The most popular procedure for young people is double eyelid surgery, which makes the eyes appear larger. At Kyoritsu, people 19 or younger made up 19% of these patients in 2018. By 2025, it was 27%.

Japanese law does not set a minimum age for cosmetic surgery. And in Shinjuku, about 3 kilometers north of Shibuya, Shonan Beauty Clinic offers double eyelid surgery to children as soon as they finish elementary school — though a parent needs to come with them and give consent.

Most patients at the clinic are older, though. "In recent years, the number of patients in their third year of junior high school is increasing," Ahmi Kim, a doctor at Shonan Beauty Clinic, told Jiji. She added that most requests for consultations come during the summer break, or before students go to high school, with Japan's school year starting in April.

Social media may be one reason cosmetic surgery is becoming more popular among Japan's young people. And there are concerns that young people sharing pictures of themselves before and after surgery may be encouraging others to feel inadequate about the way they look.
Some young people are even encouraged by their parents to get cosmetic procedures, Jiji reported.
Experts say that counseling before surgery is important to make sure young people fully understand what the procedure involves and are certain about their decision.
And not all procedures go well. The National Consumer Affairs Center of Japan received nearly 8,000 complaints about cosmetic medical procedures in 2025.
